para.text: The PRT: Particle Tracking Model Pane(s) are on the
. They are used to specify the properties of individual PRT models.
The Options tab is used to define the following properties in three groups.

li.text: If the "
Run as a separate simulation

" checkbox is checked, the PRT model will be run as a separate simulation from the groundwater flow model. However, it uses the heads and flows from the groundwater flow simulation so it is important that those heads and flows be up to date.
If the "
Use retardation factor

" checkbox is checked, the simulated particles will move more slowly than the groundwater flow. A data set will be defined for the model in which the retardation factor is specified. The velocity in each cell will be divided by the retardation factor. Retardation factors can be used to simulate the effects of linear sorption on the velocity of particles that track solute advection.
If the "
Use particle stop zones

" checkbox is checked, a data set will be defined for the model that can be used to specify zones in which particles will stop. The zone in which a particle stops is defined in a Particle Release Point (PRP) Package.
Output files

: PRT models can have track files that record the locations of particles at successive times and budget files that record budget information. Track files can be saved either as binary files or comma-separated value (CSV) files. Binary budget files record information for every cell. CSV budget summary file record a summary combining data from all the cells in a time step. Note that trackfiles can also be specified in
files. For the purposes of constructing budget files, each particle is assigned a mass of 1.
SCRATCH_BUFFER

: keyword to stage track events in a temporary (scratch) file instead of an in-memory buffer. Particle tracking results calculated during a time step are buffered, and output is deferred, until successful completion of the time step. By default, results are buffered in memory. However, for simulations in which a very large number of track events is generated during a time step, memory limits can be exceeded. In such cases, the SCRATCH_BUFFER option can be invoked to buffer results in a scratch file until successful completion of the time step. Buffering in a scratch file is typically slower than buffering in memory.
Track events
: There are several types of events that can be used as signals to save data to a track file. If none are specified, all will be recorded. If some are specified, only those will be recorded.
TRACK_RELEASE
—keyword to indicate that particle tracking output is to be written when a particle is released
TRACK_EXIT
—keyword to indicate that particle tracking output is to be written when a particle exits a grid feature (e.g. model, cell)
TRACK_SUBFEATURE_EXIT

—keyword to indicate that particle tracking output is to be written when a particle exits a sub-grid-scale feature. Such features are considered implementation details of the tracking algorithm employed for particular grid types, and reporting for exit events from such features is disabled by default. A sub-grid-scale feature might be when the PRT algorithm divides a cell into multiple parts in order to track particles in a quadtree refined grid between different levels of quadtree refinement.
TRACK_TIMESTEP
—keyword to indicate that particle tracking output is to be written at the end of each time step
TRACK_TERMINATE
—keyword to indicate that particle tracking output is to be written when a particle terminates for any reason
TRACK_WEAKSINK
—keyword to indicate that particle tracking output is to be written when a particle exits a weak sink (a cell which removes some but not all inflow from adjacent cells)
TRACK_USERTIME
—keyword to indicate that particle tracking output is to be written at user-specified times, provided as double precision values in the TRACKTIMES block.
TRACK_DROPPED
—keyword to indicate that particle tracking output is to be written when a particle is dropped to the water table via DRY_TRACKING_METHOD DROP.
Each PRT model can have one or more

. Each PRP package specifies when and where particles are released as well as a number of other options. The locations where particles are released are specified in objects. The the other properties of each PRP package aare specified in a separate

. The user can specify a name for each PRP package. The names can be up to 16 ASCII characters in length and can not contain spaces. Each package name within a PRT model must be unique. The user also specifies whether a particular PRP package is to be used in a simulation. If a package is used, input for that package will be generated for the model.
The user can specify specific times at which the locations of particles are to be recorded in any output files. The
TRACK_USERTIME
option must be active in the PRP package(s) for this option to have an effect. Those times can be specified in the table on the "
Track Times"
tab.

para.text: Budget Data by Stress Period tab

The user can specify a variety of ways to determine when the budget data is printed or saved. Data will be printed, saved, or both by combining all the methods that are specified. If nothing is specified on this tab, and a binary budget file or a CSV budget summary file is selected, budget data will be written for every time step.

li.text: Starting time
: This is the beginning time of the first stress period to which the data in the row will apply.
Ending time
: This is the ending time of the last stress period to which the data in the row will apply.
Print or Save
: The budget data can either be saved to a binary file or have a summary printed to a text file or both.
All Steps
: If the check box in a row is checked, data will be printed, saved, or both for every time step in the specified stress period or periods.
First Step
: If the check box in a row is checked, data will be printed, saved, or both for the first time step in the specified stress period or periods.
Last Step
: If the check box in a row is checked, data will be printed, saved, or both for the last time step in the specified stress period or periods.
Step Frequency
: If a number is specified, data will be printed, saved, or both at the specified step frequency in the specified stress period or periods.
Steps
: If a comma-separated list of step numbers is specified, data will be printed, saved, or both in the specified stress period or periods.
